title: Anuskkummikak
summary: Anuskkummikak is an Indigenous place name connected with the upland part of Little East Neck in Babylon, formerly also called Captain Fleet's Neck. The surviving description places the name on the upland planting ground rather than the creek or meadow.
address_label: General upland Little East Neck / Babylon area, Babylon, NY
why_this_matters: Anuskkummikak preserves a Native description of Little East Neck as planting land, linking the Babylon shoreline to foodways, seasonal work, and careful land use. Its variant spellings show how a Native agricultural term was carried into colonial records through imperfect English writing. Fields, necks, and waterways were part of connected community landscapes across Indigenous Long Island.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Anusbymonika, Anuskcomuncak, Amuskemunnica, and Wamskcumuncake. The name is interpreted as land to hoe or break up, planting land, corn fields, or plowed ground.

Wainskcumuncake is a cross-reference spelling kept with this Little East Neck / Captain Fleet's Neck entry.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names are key in the preservation of our indigenous languages, which constitute intangible heritage. Place names are important as well in preserving oral history and oral traditions.”

— Nobuhle Ndimande-Hlongwa, The role of indigenous place names in preserving living heritage of the Zulu people in KwaZulu-Natal (2016), Conclusion
whereintheworld_content: Anuskkummikak distinguishes a planting ground and adjacent meadow on the same neck. That distinction records land use, not just a place label, and keeps farming and food geography visible.
